source_policy: Original source is authoritative. Keep excerpts and metadata intact; name matches are discovery candidates, not encounters. No inference of consent, knowledge, direct contact, completed action, or continuous story time from co-mention.

coverage_policy.CURATED_FIRST_PASS: At least one source-indexed action record exists for the selected pair; second-pass action/recipient/source QA remains pending.
coverage_policy.SCENE_ANCHOR_ONLY: A source-linked scene is indexed, but action-by-action review is not certified.
coverage_policy.DISCOVERY_ONLY: Only lexical mentions were discovered; direct participation is not established.
coverage_policy.NOT_REVIEWED: No qualifying source-reviewed records in this track; never infer absence from this state.
coverage_policy.PARTIAL_SCENE_EVENTS: Only selected actions within one or more source-linked scene fragments are tagged; no claim of complete scene or episode review.

gaps.title: E06–E68 completeness
gaps.closure: Review each relevant narrative scene, including pronoun-only continuations; source evidence required.

gaps.title: Mention vs encounter
gaps.closure: Classify mention, memory, direct meeting, reported event, observed event and remote contact separately.

gaps.title: Participant graph
gaps.closure: Preserve actor, recipient, observer, bystander, present, absent and source of knowledge per independent action.

gaps.title: Multi-action source lines
gaps.closure: Split actions on a line into distinct IDs without changing or duplicating the canonical source line.

gaps.title: Request–response–stop
gaps.closure: Link initiative, request, response, refusal/objection, completion and interruption with separate evidence.

gaps.title: Visual state transitions
gaps.closure: Record garment/visibility before-after, who observed it, and whether direct contact actually occurred.

gaps.title: Emotional change evidence
gaps.closure: Previous stated mindset, trigger, explicit reaction, next supported state; unknown where evidence absent.

gaps.title: Story-time chronology
gaps.closure: Track unique encounters across continued scenes, recalls and flashbacks; prevent double counting.

gaps.title: Specialized history views
gaps.closure: Present physical/body or visual-state and writing-mechanism histories with exact source references and reviewed/pending distinction.

gaps.title: Lossless evidence rendering
gaps.closure: Render raw record details including offsets, checksum, status, review, notes, observer/recipient without flattening them.

gaps.title: Cross-track overlap
gaps.closure: One shared-scene ID; derived track memberships do not imply direct pair contact.

gaps.title: Character knowledge
gaps.closure: Know/observe/hear/recall/reported ledgers must be individual and chronological.

gaps.title: Everyday-to-relationship chain
gaps.closure: Task → request → dialogue → reaction → interruption → aftermath, only where source supports it.

gaps.title: First vs repeated milestones
gaps.closure: First, last, repeated milestones only after encounter order and action classification are verified.

gaps.title: Writing style evidence
gaps.closure: Preserve source-backed POV, dialogue rhythm, ordinary-scene pacing and callbacks; do not generalize unreviewed episodes.

gaps.title: Prediction/canon separation
gaps.closure: Store hypothetical scenarios in separate ledger; never inject them into recorded history.

gaps.title: Episode QA coverage
gaps.closure: Episode-by-track coverage states must distinguish first pass, anchor only, discovery and not reviewed.

gaps.title: Exports and signoff
gaps.closure: Filtered JSON export, episode progress and explicit reviewer certification after QA.

writing_observations.observation: Introduction → permission request → acceptance → shared painting task. Dialogue moves the ordinary activity forward.
Sleeping arrangements are discussed; departures and Dhika's reaction follow. The participants' perceptions must remain distinct.
The interaction alternates a video-call attempt and text messages; do not reclassify it as in-person co-presence.
